It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. London has been named the fifth most expensive city in Europe for a day out, with visitors spending an average of £118.37 on food, drinks, transport and sightseeing. This puts a day in the capital above the widely used £100 daily budget r ecommended for comfortable travel. The findings come from a new study by InsureandGo, which calculated the cost of a typical day out—including two meals, drinks, public transport, and entry to a top attraction— in more than 120 European cities. A costly day out The research found that other UK cities also exceed the £100 mark, including Edinburgh (£104.45), Bristol (£103.80), and Liverpool (£101.29). Mellisa Hutchins, travel cover specialist at InsureandGo, said: "Our study shows that across most of Europe, a daily budget of £100 still covers a full day of eating out and sightseeing, and in some cities across Central Europe around half that amount is plenty. "Regardless of where you’re heading, plan your budget before you go. "Check local prices for food and drinks but also look for free attractions and make the most of public transport. "One place not to cut costs is your travel insurance. "Unexpected medical bills or cancellations can easily wipe out a holiday budget, so comprehensive travel cover helps you relax and enjoy your trip. "There are still plenty of places left to discover this year, and we hope this research inspires you to visit somewhere new that aligns with your budget." Comparing cities The average day out across Europe costs £78, according to the research. However, the study found wide variation in costs, with Reykjavik, Iceland, topping the list as the most expensive city at £145.33 per day. This is more than five times the daily cost of Skopje. The top five most expensive cities in Europe were Reykjavik (£145.33), Zurich (£132.11), Basel (£125.12), Bern (£121.22), and London (£118.37). Coventry was named the most affordable UK city, with a daily cost of £67.64, well below the European average. Other UK cities close to the £100 threshold include Manchester (£98.75) and Brighton (£98.36). Budget-friendly destinations Several European cities still offer excellent value for money. Chisinau, Moldova, was the second cheapest city at £35.52 per day. Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed in third place at £38.52. Other affordable destinations under £50 per day include Tirana, Albania (£44.96), and Belgrade, Serbia (£46.99). Central European cities such as Brașov, Romania (£47.23), and Poznań, Poland (£47.51), also featured in the top 10 most affordable destinations. For travellers seeking warmer weather, Porto was the most budget-friendly option at £53.65 per day. Alicante (£55.28) and Málaga (£55.44) in Spain also made the list. Free and low-cost travel Several destinations stand out not only for their low overall costs but for specific budget-friendly features. Belgrade, for example, offers free public transport, while Skopje boasts the cheapest entry fee to a top attraction—a cable car ride to the Millennium Cross costs just £1.39. Chisinau is an ideal base for exploring Moldova’s famous wine country, with public transport costing as little as 60 pence for a return journey. Visitors to Sarajevo can enjoy lunch for just £6.59, with a three-course dinner averaging £15.36. The city’s Baščaršija quarter, known for its blend of Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian architecture, offers a rich cultural experience at an affordable price. Travel tips Ms Hutchins encouraged travellers to research their destinations in advance to get the most value from their trips. She advised looking for free attractions, making use of public transport, and prioritising travel insurance to avoid unexpected costs. She also emphasised that a daily budget of £100 remains reasonable in many European cities, though some will require more careful planning.
